title: Father of Heav’n, Whose Love Profound
description: Father of Heav’n, Whose Love Profound in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Edward Cooper wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 269.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of heav’n, whose love pro-found A ran-som for our souls has found, Be-fore Thy throne we sin-ners bend; To us Thy par-doning love ex-tend.

lines: Father of heav’n, whose love profound
A ransom for our souls has found,
Before Thy throne we sinners bend;
To us Thy pardoning love extend.
Before Thy throne we sinners bend;
To us Thy saving grace extend.
The soul is raised from sin and death,
Before Thy throne we sinners bend;
To us Thy quickening power extend.
Before Thy throne we sinners bend;
Grace, pardon, life, to us extend.

licence: Public domain: Edward Cooper died in 1833.
credits: Words by Edward Cooper (1770–1833), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
